# search answers with an index (no bodies, titles cut to 160, 8 hits, more/hint); task_get gives…

search answers with an index (no bodies, titles cut to 160, 8 hits, more/hint); task_get gives each body's first line and the fields an agent acts on; full:true gives whole records

**Context.** Claude Code gives the model a tool's `structuredContent` as JSON, so result size is context. Measured on the real database (2026-11-03):
- `search`, 20 hits: 17–35 KB, because it returned whole records with whole bodies; some older imported titles are 800–1,300 chars.
- `task_get #1` (17 records): 9.6 KB, with bodies cut to 500 chars plus every internal field.

**Decision.**
- `search` by default returns, per hit, `id`, `task_key`, `kind`, `status`, `owner` and `pointer` when set, and `title` cut to 160 chars.
  - The default limit is 8 (max 100). It fetches limit + 1, so `more: true` can say there are more.
  - One `hint` names `full: true` (whole records with bodies) and `task_get`.
- `task_get` by default leaves out `uid`, `task_id`, `position` and `created_at`. It cuts each body to its first non-empty line, at most 160 chars, with `body_truncated`. `full: true` gives the whole records.
- The record schema's required fields are now `id`, `kind`, `status`, `title`, so both lean shapes validate.

**Measured after:**
- `search`, typical: 1.75–1.8 KB for 8 hits (was 17–35 KB for 20).
- `task_get #1`: 6.9 KB (was 9.6 KB).
- `task_get #115`: 0.9 KB (was 1.4 KB).

Every body is one more call away.
